bandReport.notes: 21 questions, Q80-Q100 contiguous, no gap. Footers read (21-C), (23-C), (25-C), (27-C); foot-left TFDD-B-AGT on all four. Both seams are clean: the page before (p19, footer (19-C)) ends with Q79 complete, and the page after (p29, footer (29-C)) opens with Q101, so no question is unowned on either side. 6/5/4/6 questions per page. Page count matches the printed odd-page-only Part B sequence -- no even page and no Devanagari anywhere in this band. Content runs Biology (Q80-85), then Chemistry (Q86-100); p29 changes subject to History, consistent with Q100 being the last of a block. TRANSCRIPTION NOTES: (1) Q86, Q88, Q90 and Q91 all carry the SAME option set (I and II only / II and III only / I and III only / I, II and III) and Q87 looks identical but its (d) is 'II only' -- each was read label by label off the page and Q87's (d) was re-cropped at 8x to confirm, so this is a genuine difference and not a copy. (2) Q93 statement II is printed as 'calcium carbonate hemihydrate, called Plaster of Paris' -- chemically that should be calcium SULPHATE hemihydrate. Verified at 8x; transcribed exactly as printed, not corrected. Its statement III likewise prints 'green-coloured copper sulphate dihydrate'. Both are source oddities, flagged so nobody 'repairs' a faithful transcription. (3) Q95 (four options differing only in digits) and Q96 (options differing by one word: sodium/potassium, Glycerol/Glycol) were each re-cropped at 8-9x before being written. (4) Q85's stem runs to the page trim after the word 'not' -- the article is clipped at the right margin. All four of its OPTIONS are fully legible and complete; only the terse stem is affected. No option anywhere in this band was unreadable. (5) Pen marking is present on every page of this Series C scan (options struck through, ticks, a stray line). Ignored throughout per the brief -- none of it is recorded and none of it influenced a reading.

questions.stem: Which of the following organisms show external fertilization? I. Pigeon II. Frog III. Fish IV. Lizard
Which one of the following plant groups is characterized by having a haploid plant body?
A flower typically is composed of :
Which one of the following organelles is found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
Which one of the following is not a connective tissue in the human body?
Which one of the following is not a characteristic of an insect-pollinated plant?

options.label: D

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding oxidation numbers : I. Oxidation number of oxygen in peroxides and superoxides is assigned as -1 and -1/2 respectively. II. In all its compounds, fluorine has an oxidation number of -1. III. In a reduction half-reaction, the oxidation number of the reductant decreases. Which are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding the properties of hydrogen and water : I. Tritium, the isotope of hydrogen, is radioactive and emits low energy alpha particles. II. In the gas phase, the structure of water is linear. III. The basic principle of a hydrogen economy is the transportation and storage of energy in the form of liquid or gaseous molecular hydrogen. Which is/are NOT correct?

Consider the following statements regarding nitrogen : I. Nitrogen contains a triple bond. II. Nitrogen is a triatomic gas. III. Forces acting between nitrogen molecules are weak van der Waals forces. Which are correct?

In a dry test tube, 2 mL of HCl (0.1 N) is taken. To this, 4 mL of NaOH (0.1 N) is added. The solution is stirred well, followed by the addition of 2 drops of phenolphthalein. What will be the colour of the solution?

Consider the following statements : I. Zinc metal, when treated with both HCl (aq.) and NaOH (aq.) separately, produces molecular hydrogen. II. An aqueous copper sulphate solution cannot be kept in a zinc vessel. III. Lemon, tamarind and tomato are natural sources of citric acid, oxalic acid and tartaric acid, respectively. Which are correct?

Consider the following statements : I. A solution of iodine in ethanol known as 'tincture of iodine' is a heterogeneous mixture. II. A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture and its particles scatter a beam of light passing through it, making its path visible. III. A colloidal solution, although it appears homogeneous, is a heterogeneous mixture. Which are correct?

Consider the following statements : I. A 30% solution of hydrogen peroxide is marketed as '10 volume' H2O2. II. In the compound copper sulphate pentahydrate, all the five water molecules are hydrogen bonded. Which is/are correct?

Consider the following statements : I. The leaves of nettle, a herbaceous plant, cause painful stings when touched accidentally because of the secretion of formic acid. II. When gypsum is heated at 100 degrees C, it forms calcium carbonate hemihydrate, called Plaster of Paris. III. When moistened with water, anhydrous copper sulphate forms a green-coloured copper sulphate dihydrate. Which is/are correct?

Consider the following pairs (Chemical Reaction / Type of Chemical Reaction) : I. Fe(s) + CuSO4 (aq.) -> FeSO4 (aq.) + Cu(s) -- Displacement reaction; II. Na2SO4 (aq.) + BaCl2 (aq.) -> BaSO4(s) + 2NaCl (aq.) -- Double displacement reaction; III. Fe2O3(s) + 3CO(g) -> 2Fe(s) + 3CO2(g) -- Redox reaction; IV. 2KClO3(s) -> 2KCl(s) + 3O2(g) -- Thermal decomposition reaction. How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
What are the approximate percentages by mass of nitrogen and hydrogen respectively in urea?

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding hydrogen bonds : I. Hydrogen bonds can only form when hydrogen is bonded to oxygen, nitrogen or fluorine. II. Hydrogen bonds are intramolecular only. III. The strength of a hydrogen bond decreases with a decrease in the electronegativity of the two bonded atoms. Which is/are NOT correct?
Ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points. This is due to :

options.label: A
options.text: the presence of strong electrostatic forces between ions in the crystal lattice.

options.label: B
options.text: the weak intermolecular van der Waals forces.

options.label: C
options.text: the presence of a 'sea of delocalized electrons'.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is/are correct in respect of Portland cement? I. Adding more water (higher water-cement ratio) accelerates the initial setting time of cement. II. The addition of a small percentage of gypsum gives the desired retardation. III. Gypsum is added during manufacturing to accelerate the setting time of cement.

Consider the following pairs (Example of Colloid / Type of Colloid) : I. Cloud -- Aerosol; II. Mud -- Sol; III. Milk -- Emulsion; IV. Rubber -- Foam. How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
